dataset.name: ULB / Worldline card transactions (2013)
dataset.time_unit: Seconds since first observed transaction; not a calendar date

selection_rule: Highest uncalibrated average precision on tune period; no final-test-based selection.

benchmark_protocol.split: Ordered time quantiles: train 50%, tune 15%, calibration 15%, test 20%; tied timestamps kept together.
benchmark_protocol.calibration: Sigmoid fit on independent calibration period. Threshold from same period targets 1% alerts; actual test alert rate can differ.
benchmark_protocol.uncertainty: 150 fixed non-overlapping-block resamples (40 contiguous blocks), percentile 95% AP interval; conditional on this fitted model.
benchmark_protocol.latency: 12 local repetitions of a 256-row batch; includes feature validation and calibration; excludes network and disk.
benchmark_protocol.average_precision: scikit-learn average_precision_score; step-weighted AP, not trapezoidal PR area.

limitations: Two days of European transactions from 2013 do not establish current bank or Indian payment performance.
Original PCA fitting provenance is outside this experiment; entity identifiers and label delay are unavailable.
PCA components cannot be translated into merchant, device, customer or behavioral explanations.
Fraud labels are historical outcomes, not proof of criminal intent; scores require human review.
Exposure is the sum of historical fraud transaction amounts; it is not realized savings or recoverable loss.
Local results are not directly comparable to published random-split or Kaggle hidden-test scores.
Block bootstrap intervals describe this short test period only; few frauds and dependent events limit precision.
Protected attributes are unavailable; demographic fairness cannot be measured on this dataset.
